Mass grave of martyrs in grave condition
2014-12-02T00:00:49+06:00 | Mamun-ur-Rashid, Bogra
https://www.thedailystar.net/mass-grave-of-martyrs-in-grave-condition-52924

The premises of a memorial built at the mass grave of Liberation War martyrs on railway land beside Station Road in the town now gives the look of a garbage dumping station, as the place is now virtually occupied by land grabbers. The illegal occupies have also rented a portion of the place, making small tin-shed rooms and shops and are conducting narcotic business and other illegal activities there. On April 30 in 1971, the Pakistan army and their local collaborators killed at least 20 innocent people by shooting and bayonet charge at the spot, locals said. The martyrs including Abdus Sattar and his brothers Abdul Kader and Abdus Salam, Abdul Gani and his son Abdul Motin Shuja, Mohor Ali Sheikh and 14 unidentified ones were buried in the mass grave, said Lutfar Rahman, former commander of Bogra municipality unit of Muktijoddha Sangsad. Abdul Wadud, younger brother of the first three, was also taken to the killing spot but he managed to escape, Lutfar quoted Wadud as saying. The victims' family members later traced out the mass grave and the local administration built a memorial there in honour of the martyrs. "But the land grabbers occupied the graveyard and its adjacent areas, showing utter disrespect to the brave sons of the soil," said Ruhul Amin Bablu, district unit commander of Muktijoddha Sangsad. Contacted, Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) of Bogra Md Khorshed Alam said, "Following the order of the deputy commissioner, we have sent a letter to the mayor of Bogra municipality to clear the land from the grabbers. We are working with railway department and municipality to free the mass grave of the Liberation War martyrs."
